pages.says: Iran's foreign minister says the argument for dropping Iran's no-bomb doctrine is strong, while insisting policy hasn't changed, and nobody knows where its near-weapons-grade uranium is.
pages.weakest: Their Shenzhen declaration with America on 19 November held that a nuclear war cannot be won, and did not mention Iran (No. 168).

pages.says: Denmark expelled Russia's defence attaché after its intelligence service said Russia hired gang members to kill a Ukrainian-American rapper outside Copenhagen.
pages.weakest: two further men, not accused of taking part, were later drawn into the inquiry.

pages.says: Wong met Li Qiang in Beijing and the two countries signed transport and green-industry pacts and mapped their AI rules against each other, with little change for households yet.
pages.weakest: Singapore's statement adds a joint line on the right to freedom of passage in international waterways.

pages.says: Real urushi lacquer on chopsticks is rarer than labels suggest, and a Wakasa maker sells honestly labelled pairs it will re-lacquer, from about ¥5,500.
pages.weakest: The white-label truth is on the label.
pages.reason: Opening never says what is new; headline hard to parse; middle wanders; lead with plastic-paint point and how to tell.
pages.fixed: New headline and opening on plastic paint vs urushi and how to read the coat label; cut the white-label line, 1973 origin rules and Obama anecdote; makers' prices in one tiered paragraph.

pages.says: Under a new US rule TSMC has stopped taking advanced chip orders from unlicensed Chinese designers, holding them to older production lines, though the cost to TSMC looks small.
pages.weakest: The American rule behind it was covered on our Singapore page in No. 168.

pages.says: Thinking Machines released a free AI model that runs offline on a well-equipped laptop and roughly matches the desk's usual reference model, with real flaws.
pages.weakest: Of 26.4 billion parameters, only 3.4 billion work on each word-piece.
pages.reason: Paragraphs three and four assume specialist vocabulary never explained; say what laptop, how fast, what it is good and bad at; one benchmark explained.
pages.fixed: Jargon cut or glossed; one paragraph on what hardware is needed, one on speed in plain units, one benchmark (SWE-bench Verified) explained; experts/NVFP4/BrowseComp removed.

pages.says: Grado's first wireless open-back headphones in four years cost US$329, last 60+ hours and still play through a cable, but aren't yet sold in Singapore and nobody has reviewed them.
pages.weakest: The spec sheet lists 38 ohms, 104dB at one milliwatt, 16Hz–34kHz.

pages.says: A never-polished 1952 Patek 2499 made HK$34.2 million in Hong Kong, far above estimate and Meridian's wrong call, on a day when independent watchmakers also sold well above estimate.
pages.weakest: Vintage Rolex was cooler: a Paul Newman Daytona 6263 made HK$4,826,000.

pages.says: The new Hunger Games prequel took $56 million on its first day and looks set for about $120 million over the weekend, comfortably past the $100 million call.
pages.weakest: Warner Bros' The Cat in the Hat added $1.6 million.

pages.says: A large US study finds teens and parents usually disagree about a child's mental-health problems, so ask a child directly and on her own.
pages.weakest: Here the team, from UC San Diego, the Laureate Institute in Tulsa and Oregon Health & Science University, derived DSM-5 diagnoses

pages.says: Most English secondary pupils bite nails, pick skin or pull hair; about one in eight are distressed by it, and habit-reversal therapy is the standard treatment.
pages.weakest: Screens and grey matter: a University of Eastern Finland MRI study of 44 teenagers

pages.says: In last week's sell-off investors ran to long-dated US Treasuries while gold and bitcoin both fell, and the desk's four leans for the coming week still point lower.
pages.weakest: PIMCO Income: Singapore-dollar hedged class 1 week −0.12, 1 month −0.05 ...

pages.says: Central banks keep buying gold slowly while fast fund money sets the price, and next week brings US inflation data and a short Thanksgiving week.
pages.weakest: Inside the Fund · The All-World Fund's Japan Bet Meets The BoJ
pages.reason: Repeats p14 (central-bank gold in p14's Sceptic; Fed/BoJ dates on both); Japan box not about Japan; jargon dashboard; 2021 bar clashes with 2010-21 average.

pages.says: Foraging is having a moment thanks to TikTok's Alexis Nikole Nelson; the rules vary from permissive Sweden to strict Singapore, and Japan records the poisonings.
pages.weakest: 15,747 Members of foraging groups on Meetup

pages.says: A forager's kit is a knife, a basket and a field guide, from a US$23 Opinel to a £160 Sussex trug, and plant apps help but can't be trusted alone.
pages.weakest: Niwaki's forged hori-hori is on pre-order, with dispatch not before 14 May 2027.

pages.says: Foraging kills through look-alikes, from hemlock to daffodils picked as garlic chives (17 deaths in Japan in a decade); in Singapore a beginner starts with guided walks.
pages.weakest: Practice then goes abroad: Wild Food UK teaches at more than 30 venues

pages.says: A small Japanese trial suggests light elastic-band training improves artery linings in older adults, possibly through irisin, though the evidence is thin.
pages.weakest: Also on the desk, too much of a good thing: in a University of São Paulo mouse study

pages.says: From Monday Singapore Airlines flies daily to Sydney's new curfew-free Western Sydney airport, though there is no train to the city yet.
pages.weakest: New route Lounge Points

pages.says: Air New Zealand's Singapore–Christchurch flight now runs all year with refitted 787 cabins, so families can fly nonstop to the South Island in the June holidays.
pages.weakest: Further back, Premium Economy seats are 19 inches wide with 41 inches of pitch.

pages.says: Shirakawa-go will light up its snowbound village on four January evenings, open only to visitors who booked, and the last ways in open on 26 November and 1 December.
pages.weakest: Reddit, TripAdvisor and FlyerTalk could not be read for this piece

pages.says: Takayama is the easy base for Shirakawa-go, reached by overnight flight to Nagoya and the Hida train, but JR's area pass charges a 12-year-old the adult fare.
pages.weakest: Ropeway pause. The Shin-Hotaka Ropeway closes for maintenance from 24 to 27 November.

pages.says: A list of upcoming Singapore concerts, led by Stray Kids in March, and Japanese events worth flying for, with booking notes.
pages.weakest: Still unpriced: Kenshi Yonezu, KATSEYE, Maroon 5 and Freya Skye ...

pages.says: Casa Vostra's Wisma Atria branch now takes bookings and sells square pizza slices, and an airport mala shop gets a good first review plus a correction on its opening date.

pages.says: Jiangsu schools have pushed back their gates after reports of fifteen-hour school days, but earlier limits were dodged by renaming early study.
pages.weakest: A parents' account run by the Qianjiang Evening News drew more than 400 comments

pages.says: Other Chinese cities are also moving start times, but seventy years of reducing the burden have only moved the hours, which may now slide into the evening.
pages.weakest: Fudan's Liu Hong calls the pressure systemic.
